label: Loss aversion
description: A ₹5,000 loss feels roughly twice as large as an equivalent gain. Manifests as fear of a bad purchase, resale anxiety and status loss.

label: Price anchoring
description: The sticker price, the neighbour's purchase price and the EMI per month become anchors. '₹999 per month' can feel cheaper than '₹24,000'.

label: Bandwagon effect
description: Adoption rises when it becomes visible in the reference group. Viral WhatsApp forwards and wedding-season displays are strong cues.

label: Authority bias
description: Trust flows to titled people and uniforms more than to anonymous reviews, especially outside metros.

label: In-group trust
description: Language, caste, religion, region and occupation shape who is believed. This is a structural advantage, not a personal failing.

label: Availability heuristic
description: One fire, one fraud, one accident on the news outweighs ten thousand quiet successes. Local WhatsApp video is the strongest form.

label: Optimism bias
description: Young, aspirational buyers underestimate maintenance, loan and health shocks. 'Mera number kab aayega' is a plan.

label: Zero-sum thinking
description: Markets, jobs and opportunities are read as fixed pies: the app is stealing the kirana's customer; the migrant is taking the job.

label: Fatalism / chalta hai
description: A coping grammar that absorbs dysfunction as normal. It reduces complaint and adoption of fixes, but also cushions disappointment.

label: Status signalling
description: Visible consumption is social communication: the car in the driveway, the phone at the wedding, the English-medium school.

label: Scarcity mindset
description: Decisions are made from the current wallet, not the annual balance sheet. A ₹2,000 EMI can be unaffordable even at a ₹1 lakh salary.

label: Ambiguity aversion
short: I don't understand it, so no
description: New categories with unclear ownership, warranty or resale are penalised. The dealer and the local repairman reduce ambiguity.

label: Confirmation bias
description: People seek evidence that fits existing beliefs. Once a brand is labelled 'Chinese' or 'anti-Hindu' or 'elite', facts rarely move it.

label: Recency bias
description: The latest video, price cut or scam headline dominates a longer track record. Social feeds are built to exploit this.

label: Just-world belief
description: Success is attributed to merit, failure to character. It makes structural problems invisible and victim-blaming easy.

label: Tall poppy / envy
description: Visible success invites suspicion and schadenfreude. It punishes early adopters who display new status symbols.
